title: Meet Ana-Karina De Paula Allen, who clashed with Nessie at the RHOL reunion
excerpt: She used to work at Vogue
content:
Ana-Karina de Paula Allen made a surprise appearance at part two of The Real Housewives of London season two reunion, and she didn’t come quietly. The season two guest joined the cast on stage and claimed Juliet Mayhew had wanted to freeze her out of the group. Juliet Angus backed her up, which made the whole thing even messier.

Viewers haven’t seen much of her on the show, but off camera she’s a mum of four with a seriously impressive career in fashion and luxury. Here’s everything we know about Ana-Karina from Real Housewives of London.

She grew up in Brazil

Ana-Karina grew up in Brazil and lived in the United States and Italy before settling in the UK. When she arrived, her plan was to become a journalist.

Her career started in a far less glamorous place than Vogue. Her first job was selling advertising for Odeon’s cinema magazine, which meant cold-calling local businesses around its cinema in Huddersfield.

From Huddersfield to British Vogue

From there she moved into publishing, first at Hearst and then at Condé Nast. She worked her way up to commercial director at British Vogue, specialising in jewellery, so she spent years at the business end of one of the most famous magazines in the world.

She also helped bring watches and jewellery onto Net-a-Porter, and she’s since gone on to work with Tiffany & Co. She describes her Tiffany role as more diplomatic than celebrity or influencer-led. Her job is creating experiences for the brand’s private clients, which explains how comfortable she seemed holding her own on the reunion stage.

She’s also had a go at running her own businesses. She’s run an influencer agency, works as an angel investor, and was a director of House of Holland, the label founded by designer Henry Holland, from 2018. That company has since been dissolved.

She’s a big name in fashion philanthropy

Ana-Karina is a patron of the British Fashion Council Foundation, which supports emerging British designers. She regularly turns up at the big industry events, including the BFC/Vogue Designer Fashion Fund winner announcement in 2025, and she’s hosted events for her fellow patrons, including a studio visit to sustainable denim brand E.L.V. Denim.

She also sits on London’s Air Ambulance Philanthropy Board, which raises money for the capital’s air ambulance service.

She’s a mum of four

Ana-Karina has four children, and she’s built most of her career while raising them. She’s spoken openly about how hard that can be, saying “every meaningful choice has a cost,” and she believes ambitious women are often pushed to hide the sacrifices they make. She keeps her relationship out of the spotlight, so there isn’t much public information about her partner.

She’s just landed a magazine cover

Before her reunion moment, Ana-Karina was already making headlines as the cover star of a special edition of The Guide’s Lifestyle Compendium Vol. 5. The cover story looks back at her career and focuses on how much trust and relationships have mattered to her along the way. Given what she said about Juliet Mayhew at the reunion, viewers might find that quite telling.

The shoot was very luxurious too. In one look she wore a £1,470 Patrick McDowell blazer with a pair of Tiffany & Co. earrings worth £34,900.

To celebrate the cover, she co-hosted a private dinner at Isabel in Mayfair, with guests from across fashion, luxury, design and media.
